units.title: Continuity of an integral with a moving observable and law
units.statement: Let T be a topological parameter space and X a compact topological space with a measurable structure in which open sets are measurable. If F:T×X→ℝ is jointly continuous and t↦μ_t is a continuous curve of probability measures in the weak topology, then t↦∫F(t,x) μ_t(dx) is continuous.
assumptions: The parameter space is topological. The compact topological state space has measurable open sets.
The real observable F is jointly continuous, and t↦μ_t is continuous in the weak topology of probability measures.

steps.title: Freeze the observable
steps.text: At a fixed t the function F(t,·) is continuous and bounded on the compact state space, so weak convergence controls its integral.

steps.title: Bound the moving part
steps.text: Joint continuity and compactness control the observable difference uniformly near t. The integrating measure has mass one.

steps.title: Add the two limits
steps.text: The moving part tends to zero, leaving the limit of the frozen integral.
steps.lean: Split the integral and use addition of limits.

units.lean_statement: The folded signature specifies the domain and hypotheses.
units.lean_proof: The folded proof follows the calculation above.
units.boundary: Compactness controls the changing observable uniformly. Weak continuity controls integration of the frozen observable.
